name_note: GTDB splits the classical Sutterella wadsworthensis into several species-level lineages, of which s__Sutterella wadsworthensis_A is one; published work refers simply to Sutterella wadsworthensis.

sentences.text: S. wadsworthensis has been recovered from human feces both in clinical cases of gastrointestinal disorders and from a healthy individual.
A study reported that S. wadsworthensis preferentially bound mucus and human extracellular matrix proteins and induced interleukin-8 in enterocytes, though its pro-inflammatory activity was modest.
The same work described members of the genus Sutterella as widely prevalent commensals, with no difference detected in prevalence between pediatric IBD or celiac patients and healthy controls.

Reported associations are mixed: one fecal transplant trial found S. wadsworthensis enriched in ulcerative colitis patients not achieving remission, while a metagenomic study reported it depleted in adults with asthma.
